question: For a ticket whose build commit predates its journaled forward BUILDME crossing (68f563403c8f today, and every other pre-journal ticket that re-crosses), how do I give hollow a true pre-build commit — (a) a pre_build sha carried on the crossing, (b) revert-and-recommit the build behind a fresh crossing, or (c) something else?
why_it_blocks: 68f's build landed in edb4e137 BEFORE its journaled forward BUILDME crossing (the original crossing predates the crossing journal; the retreat-and-recross I did today to give hollow a record put the BUILDME crossing at 15:12, after the build). hollow.py derives pre-build as the last commit before that crossing = HEAD, so all four writes_to files read UNWRIT and the reading measured nothing (rc=1, 'a measurement of the empty set is not a pass'); clearance refuses PROVED on hollow_nothing_measured. The same shape waits on every pre-journal ticket that re-crosses. Options I see: (a) the forward BUILDME crossing may carry pre_build=<sha> (recorded on the journal entry at the crossing, read by hollow instead of rev-list --before) — a small tester+transitions change under this ticket or a new one; (b) retreat to TICKETME, commit the five files back to their 8cdc2440 bytes, cross BUILDME, commit the build again, rehearse, PROVEME, hollow — the record then reads in build order but the commit hook reseals codemother's proofs red in between; (c) the retreat-and-recross itself is the defect and pre-journal builds get a different door.
